### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in NRF1 (HGNC:1385) (HGNC:1385) —DISRUPTS→ NRF1 (HGNC:1385); NRF1 (HGNC:1385) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial dysfunction (GO:0008152); NRF1 (HGNC:1385) —DECREASES→ Cellular stress response (GO:0006950); Mitochondrial dysfunction (GO:0008152) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Cellular stress response (GO:0006950) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Loss-of-function variants in NRF1 lead to impaired mitochondrial function and cellular stress, contributing to both intellectual disability (Disease A) and hearing impairment (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NRF1 in individuals with only one of the two diseases, without any evidence of the other, or if NRF1 variants are found to be protective against one of the conditions. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting NRF1-mediated pathways or downstream effectors of mitochondrial function and cellular stress could offer therapeutic strategies for both intellectual disability and hearing loss.

#### 2. Usher syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.448)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** Causative variant in MYO7A (HGNC:7795) —DISRUPTS→ MYO7A (HGNC:7795); MYO7A (HGNC:7795) —DISRUPTS→ Photoreceptor cell development (GO:0021995); Photoreceptor cell development (GO:0021995) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis Pigmentosa (HP:0000547); Causative variant in MYO7A (HGNC:7795) —DISRUPTS→ MYO7A (HGNC:7795); MYO7A (HGNC:7795) —DISRUPTS→ Inner ear hair cell development (GO:0035274); Inner ear hair cell development (GO:0035274) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Mutations in MYO7A disrupt both photoreceptor cell development (leading to Retinitis Pigmentosa) and inner ear hair cell development (leading to hearing impairment in Usher syndrome), highlighting a shared critical role for this gene in the development of these mechanosensory cells.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of MYO7A in photoreceptor vs. inner ear hair cells that do not share critical regulatory components or downstream effectors. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in MYO7A in the general population that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYO7A in sensory cell development could lead to therapeutic strategies that target common downstream pathways to ameliorate both visual and auditory deficits in patients with these conditions.

#### 3. hearing loss, autosomal dominant 82  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.389)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** ATP2B2 (HGNC:956) —DISRUPTS→ calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887); calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); CABP2 (HGNC:14926) —DISRUPTS→ calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887); calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Disruption of calcium homeostasis by mutations in ATP2B2 leads to developmental delay (MONDO:0013963), while disruption of the same calcium homeostasis pathway by mutations in CABP2 leads to hearing impairment (hearing loss, autosomal dominant 82).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ATP2B2 do not affect calcium homeostasis, or that mutations in CABP2 do not impact calcium homeostasis in relevant cell types. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 exomes show no common variants in ATP2B2 or CABP2 that are clearly pathogenic.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of calcium homeostasis in these distinct rare diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate calcium signaling to treat both developmental delay and hearing loss.

#### 4. macrothrombocytopenia and granulocyte inclusions with or without nephritis or sensorineural hearing loss  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.385)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYH9 (HGNC:7894) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet formation and function (GO:0007574); Platelet formation and function (GO:0007574) —LEADS_TO→ Macrothrombocytopenia (HP:0001883); Platelet formation and function (GO:0007574) —LEADS_TO→ Nephritis (HP:0000102); Platelet formation and function (GO:0007574) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405). Mutations in MYH9 lead to a disruption in platelet formation and function, resulting in macrothrombocytopenia. This disruption also affects other cellular processes, contributing to the development of nephritis and sensorineural hearing loss, which are characteristic features of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of MYH9 mutations in individuals diagnosed with either MONDO:0013963 or MONDO:0015912, or the identification of distinct causal genes with no overlap in functional pathways, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in MYH9 (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) that are implicated in these diseases would suggest the proposed mechanism is incorrect.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYH9 in these distinct but overlapping disease phenotypes could pave the way for targeted therapies that address the underlying molecular defect, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions. For instance, therapies aimed at improving platelet production or mitigating kidney and auditory damage could be explored.

#### 5. Usher syndrome type 1B  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.375)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** CABP2 (HGNC:1374) —DISRUPTS→ Inner ear hair cell development (GO:0001745); MYO7A (HGNC:7774) —DISRUPTS→ Inner ear hair cell development (GO:0001745); Inner ear hair cell development (GO:0001745) —LEADS_TO→ Hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000334); Hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000334) —LEADS_TO→ Deafness (HP:0000365); Hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000334) —LEADS_TO→ Vestibular dysfunction (HP:0007290). Mutations in both CABP2 (associated with MONDO:0013963) and MYO7A (associated with Usher syndrome type 1B) disrupt the development and function of inner ear hair cells, ultimately leading to deafness and vestibular dysfunction.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of CABP2 and MYO7A that do not converge on hair cell development or mechanotransduction, or demonstration of functional redundancy where mutations in one gene do not impact the other's pathway. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of CABP2 or MYO7A that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream effects of CABP2 and MYO7A mutations on hair cell function could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially focusing on common pathways involved in hair cell regeneration or protection.

#### 6. autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.370)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** CABP2 mutation (MONDO:0010860) —DISRUPTS→ CABP2 (HGNC:2064); CABP2 (HGNC:2064) —DECREASES→ Inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000320); Inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000320) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 4 (HP:0000365); MYO15A mutation (MONDO:0013963) —DISRUPTS→ MYO15A (HGNC:13963); MYO15A (HGNC:13963) —DECREASES→ Inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000320); Inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (GO:0000320) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss 3 (HP:0000365). Mutations in CABP2 (n1) and MYO15A (n5) both lead to dysfunction in the crucial pathway of inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction (n3), ultimately causing distinct but mechanistically related forms of hearing loss (n4 and n7).

**How to falsify it:** If genetic screening reveals that mutations in CABP2 and MYO15A do not segregate with the respective hearing loss phenotypes in affected families, or if experimental studies demonstrate independent, non-overlapping functional roles for these genes in hair cell mechanotransduction, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Identification of common variants (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in the coding regions of CABP2 or MYO15A that are not associated with hearing loss.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on inner ear hair cell mechanotransduction pathways for both CABP2 and MYO15A provides a potential therapeutic target. Strategies aimed at restoring or compensating for the function of this pathway could offer benefits for patients with either type of hearing loss.

#### 7. hearing loss, autosomal dominant 90  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.329)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9662360)

**Proposed mechanism:** CABP2 (HGNC:15801) —DISRUPTS→ Inner Ear Hair Cell Function (GO:0043467); Inner Ear Hair Cell Function (GO:0043467) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing Impairment (HP:0000365); MYO3A (HGNC:7745) —DISRUPTS→ Inner Ear Hair Cell Function (GO:0043467); Inner Ear Hair Cell Function (GO:0043467) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal Inner Ear Development (HP:0011086); Abnormal Inner Ear Development (HP:0011086) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital Glaucoma (HP:0000501). Both CABP2 and MYO3A are crucial for the proper function and development of inner ear hair cells. Haploinsufficiency of CABP2 leads to hearing impairment, while loss-of-function mutations in MYO3A disrupt hair cell function and contribute to abnormal inner ear development, ultimately causing congenital glaucoma.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in CABP2 and MYO3A affect entirely distinct cellular pathways with no downstream overlap in inner ear development or hair cell function, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: A common (AF > 0.01) loss-of-function variant in either CABP2 or MYO3A in gnomAD that is not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared mechanism could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both hearing loss and congenital glaucoma by targeting common pathways involved in inner ear development and hair cell function.
